newsitem.title: UK: Britain launches vision of electronic government.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches vision of electronic government.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday announced plans for electronic government which would give the public and business better access to services 24 hours a day using the latest information technology.
The services would include information on collecting taxes, granting licences, administering regulations, paying grants and benefits as well as collecting and analysing statistics.
Roger Freeman, Minister for Public Service, said the systems would be easy to use and would increase access to government.
"It will provide more information, make it more readily accessible and at the convenience of the user," he told a news conference to present the proposals.
Freeman said the plans were the beginning of a move towards a paperless government offering a simpler and more responsive service.
One service, "Direct Access Government", will provide forms from all the main government departments which can be printed from the screen.

Referring to similar projects in Australia, New Zealand, Singapore and the United States, the minister said the proposals would also improve Britain's competitiveness by giving businesses better access to government information.
